Bootstrap confidence band for the exact net-benefit curve

Source: R/fn_net_benefit.R
nb_exact_ci.Rd

Percentile bootstrap confidence limits for nb_exact, following the extensions of Vickers et al. (2008). Resampling is stratified by outcome by default: presences and absences are resampled with replacement separately so \(n_1\) and \(n_0\) – and therefore the prevalence case weights (reweight) – stay fixed. This keeps the interval consistent with the prevalence-invariant estimand, propagating only the sampling noise in the within-class positive rates rather than in the sample's own prevalence.

Usage

nb_exact_ci(
  truth,
  prob,
  pi,
  pt,
  B = 999,
  level = 0.8,
  side = c("lower", "both"),
  stratified = TRUE,
  cores = NULL
)

Arguments

truth

Outcomes coded 1 (presence) / 0 (absence).

prob

Predicted probabilities, same length as truth. These are assumed honest (held-out or cross-validated); the band quantifies precision, not optimism, and applies no overfit correction.

pi

Target landscape prevalence in (0, 1).

pt

Numeric vector of threshold probabilities.

B

Number of bootstrap replicates. Default 999.

level

Confidence level. Default 0.8.

side

"lower" (default) for a one-sided lower band, or "both" for a two-sided interval.

stratified

Resample within outcome classes (default TRUE) or over all observations (FALSE).

cores

Number of worker processes. Defaults to three quarters of the detected cores (at least one), capped at B.

Value

A data frame with one row per pt: the threshold pt, the point estimate nb, and lower (plus upper when side = "both").

Details

Only a lower band is returned by default. In decision-curve analysis the operative question is whether the model is at least as good as the best default strategy (treat-all or treat-none), so the decision-relevant uncertainty is the downside; an upper limit changes no decision. Use side = "both" for a two-sided interval.

Bootstrap replicates are evaluated with mclapply, which forks on Unix-alikes and falls back to serial execution on Windows. For reproducible parallel runs set RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG") and a seed before calling.

References

Vickers AJ, Cronin AM, Elkin EB, Gonen M (2008). Extensions to decision curve analysis, a novel method for evaluating diagnostic tests, prediction models and molecular markers. BMC Med Inform Decis Mak 8:53.
